PERSON.definition: A human person represented in the governed semantic field.

ISO.definition: A distinct identity/state/origin-pattern object loaded through EGO or a related identity runtime.

AI_SYSTEM.definition: A named artificial-intelligence role, engine, evaluator, profiler, or governed model-facing subsystem.

OS.definition: A named orchestration, interface, runtime, continuity, or creative operating-system layer.

ENGINE.definition: A bounded mechanism that transforms state, evidence, memory, identity, routing, or execution.

MODULE.definition: A reusable component within a larger system.

PROJECT.definition: A bounded body of work with a name, purpose, artifacts, and development history.

PROTOCOL.definition: An ordered interaction or execution contract.

LAW.definition: A governing invariant, prohibition, permission, or required behavior.

CONCEPT.definition: A named explanatory, symbolic, architectural, or analytical idea.

ARTIFACT.definition: A concrete generated or preserved object such as a seed, packet, benchmark, resume, report, or export.

EVENT.definition: A dated occurrence, transition, discovery, build, incident, or migration.

GOD_SYSTEM.definition: A named governance or specialist system in the Jarvis God System architecture.

CONNECTOR.definition: A bridge to a service, repository, database, model, runtime, or external interface.

REGISTRY.definition: An authoritative or derived index of identities, addresses, objects, or relationships.

GOVERNANCE.definition: A governed decision, validation, authority, or lifecycle structure not better represented as a law or protocol.

MEMORY.definition: A memory tier, store, continuity object, archive, or retrieval surface.

MEDIA_REFERENCE.definition: A media work, character, motif, or reference used as a governed symbolic or design source.

UNKNOWN.definition: A discovered object whose top-level category has not yet survived review.

laws: One object has one primary category and may have many tags.
Subcategory may remain unresolved without blocking identity.
Classification never creates canon by itself.
Curated classification overrides inference and preserves the inference receipt.
People and private relationships are never exported publicly merely because a scanner discovered a name.
